module_title: Newly Defined Crimes: Mob Lynching, Snatching, and Organized Crime
introduction: This intermediate tier explores the entirely new categories of crimes defined in the BNS that did not exist in the IPC. It covers the legal definitions of Mob Lynching, Snatching, Organized Crime, and the controversial Hit and Run law.

core_concepts.title: Mob Lynching (Section 103(2) BNS)
core_concepts.description:
For the first time, Mob Lynching is codified as a distinct crime.
- Definition: When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on grounds of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief, or any other similar ground.
- Punishment: Punishable with life imprisonment or death, and fine. (The liability is joint and absolute for all members of the mob).

core_concepts.title: Snatching (Section 304 BNS)
core_concepts.description:
Under the IPC, snatching a mobile phone or chain was often prosecuted as 'Theft' (IPC 379) or 'Robbery', which sometimes created judicial ambiguity regarding the element of force.
- BNS specifies 'Snatching' as a distinct offense: Theft becomes snatching if the offender, to commit theft, suddenly or quickly or forcibly seizes or secures any movable property from any person. Punishable with up to 3 years.

core_concepts.title: Hit and Run Law (Section 106(2) BNS)
core_concepts.description:
A highly debated provision that sparked nationwide protests by truck drivers.
- The Rule: Causing death by rash and negligent driving (not amounting to culpable homicide) carries a max penalty of 5 years (Sec 106(1)). HOWEVER, if the driver escapes the scene AND fails to report the incident to a police officer or magistrate soon after, the punishment jumps to a maximum of **10 years imprisonment** and a fine (Sec 106(2)).

core_concepts.title: Organized Crime (Section 111 BNS)
core_concepts.description:
Previously, organized crime was tackled by special state laws like MCOCA (Maharashtra) or UAPA. BNS brings it into the general penal code.
- Definition: Any continuing unlawful activity (kidnapping, extortion, land grabbing, financial scams, cyber-crime) by an individual acting alone or in a syndicate, using violence, threat, or coercion for financial/material benefit.
- Punishment: If it results in death, the punishment is death or life imprisonment. Otherwise, 5 years to life.

important_entities.name: Terrorist Act (Section 113 BNS)
important_entities.key_fact: Terrorism is now defined in the general penal code.
important_entities.significance: Previously handled almost exclusively under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). BNS Section 113 defines a terrorist act as any act intended to threaten the unity, integrity, sovereignty, or economic security of India, or strike terror in the people. It specifically includes the smuggling of counterfeit Indian paper currency and damage to monetary stability.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Many believe that moving the victim to the hospital absolves the driver under Sec 106(2). The law explicitly requires the driver to **report the incident to a Police Officer or Magistrate**. Merely running away to escape mob fury without reporting it still triggers the aggravated 10-year penalty.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To qualify as Mob Lynching under BNS 103(2), the group MUST be 5 or more people, AND the murder must be motivated by identity (caste, race, personal belief, etc.). A mob of 4 is just regular murder.

exam_strategy_tips: If a Judiciary exam asks 'Under which section of the BNS is Snatching defined separately from Theft?', the answer is **Section 304 BNS**.
